Energy Secretary Chris Wright says hydrocarbons aren’t running out—we’ve barely scratched the surface. The biggest energy innovations in the coming decades will likely come from oil, gas, and coal.  ow.ly/TEKA50Z0owm

Video

Utah Fits All helps families access educational options beyond their assigned public schools—but demand far outpaces funding. The constitution sets a floor for education, not a ceiling. Lawmakers should expand choice. 

ow.ly/Hrue50Z0kP2

Asylum legal entries are down 99.9%. Student visas, family visas, and H‑1B applications have cratered. 

@MrRBourne is joined by Cato’s @David_J_Bier to examine how President Trump’s executive actions have blocked more legal immigrants than illegal ones, and why the president’s stated support for legal immigration doesn’t match his policy record.
 
Listen to Cato Podcast on Spotify, Apple, and our website!
 
Spotify: ow.ly/6Lfh50Z0q8P 
Apple: ow.ly/aLy050Z0q8V 
Website: ow.ly/htgX50Z0q8Z

School choice is expanding fast—70+ programs across 30+ states. 

But passing a law isn’t enough: weak design creates waitlists, red tape, and lost opportunities. 

@ColleenHroncich outlines best practices to make educational freedom durable.
ow.ly/uM9250Z0aO5

More than 75 years after NATO’s founding, is a US withdrawal from Germany warranted? What are the likely consequences? Can the administration sustain a burden-shift to Europe? 

Join our panel of distinguished experts on transatlantic security to discuss these questions. 

Featuring: 
🔹 @LianaFix, Senior Fellow for Europe, Council on Foreign Relations
🔹 @jekavanagh, Senior Fellow & Director of Military Analysis at Defense Priorities
🔹 @JustinTLogan, Director of Defense and Foreign Policy Studies

Congress’s refusal to correct its past mistakes and legalize immigration has forced states and local governments to deal with the fallout of illegal immigration, says Cato’s @David_J_Bier. 

Watch his testimony before the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement: piped.video/UeRdruJGy2g

Video

Ayn Rand on monopolies: free markets—not regulators—are what keep monopolies in check. 

A genuinely free market, with low barriers to entry, makes it nearly impossible for any one player to dominate indefinitely.

The global economy has changed dramatically since Section 122 was enacted in the 1970s — and the current US balance of payments shows no sign of the "fundamental international payments problems" the law was designed to address, explain Cato’s @clark_packard and @AlfredCObregon in their new study.

ow.ly/9JrE50Z0qox

Human liberty and energy are the two forces that built the modern world, says Energy Secretary @SecretaryWright. 

Watch his full remarks at the Cato Institute on the current state of energy policy — and the revolutions to come.
piped.video/KGmzgrYNSKk

Video

“The great success of Fairfax, Virginia, highlights the value of immigration to the country.” — Cato's Director of Immigration Studies @David_J_Bier, testifying before the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement.

Video

"If you have institutions, culture, and education — you will not be poor." – Secretary of Energy @SecretaryWright shared a powerful and personal message at the Cato Institute event.

Watch the full conversation: piped.video/KGmzgrYNSKk

Join @thomaschattwill for a discussion with Cato research fellow @Rhetors_of_York about the existential crisis facing American liberalism, and how we might move beyond the current impasse toward a more integrated and resilient public square. nitter.net/i/broadcasts/1NGaraYQn…

Government made it too hard to build homes — and tariffs made it more expensive. 

That’s why housing is so expensive. The fix: legalize more housing, speed up permits, open up land, and end trade barriers. Cato's @sslivinski explains.

Video

Energy affordability starts with getting government out of the way. 

Cutting red tape and liberalizing federal permitting lets markets deliver cheaper, more abundant energy for American families. 

Check out the Cato Institute Handbook on Affordability to learn more:
ow.ly/ulE350YYnsB

"Capitalists” aren't conspiring against workers — and the zero-sum narrative is wrong. But people still worried about a declining “labor share” should stop blaming corporations and start fixing all the government policies that discourage hiring, trap workers in jobs, and block mobility, explains Cato's @scottlincicome. 

ow.ly/2vCA50Z0bio

Join us for a conversation with @JohnHCochrane, @DavidRMalpass, and @ocampo_emilio discussing the benefits of dollarization to Latin American countries with a history of bad monetary policy, why dollarization in the Americas would be good for the United States, and how adopting the dollar as the legal currency has worked out in Panama, Ecuador, and El Salvador. The speakers will discuss ways of dollarizing and why that reform is especially relevant to Argentina and Venezuela today.
nitter.net/i/

Consumer goods are less affordable today than a year ago—the first time this has happened in three years. But there are solutions. 

Cato scholars have developed 100+ policy ideas to defuse inflation and lower the cost of living: cato.org/handbook-affordabil…

Over 70 educational freedom programs now operate across more than 30 states — a remarkable expansion of school choice in America. 

Cato's @ColleenHroncich identifies the five key components every successful program needs and shows how states like Florida and Arizona are leading the way.

ow.ly/fSuA50YXRfv

President Trump is right to withdraw troops from Germany and from Europe, explain Cato’s @JustinTLogan and American Ideas Institute’s Sumantra Maitra:

“German and broader European security do not require American power in theater by the division.”
